facts.text: I've been getting short of breath.
Over the past month it has been getting steadily worse.
Before that, I'd been getting breathless on exertion for about a year.
I've been getting more and more tired.
Recently I've become breathless when I lie flat.

facts.item: waking at night short of breath
facts.text: Recently I've been waking up at night short of breath.
Recently both my legs have been swelling, more and more.
I've been treated with furosemide, 40 mg twice a day.
It hasn't made me any better.
I was also given enalapril, 5 mg twice a day.
It didn't make me better.
It made me dizzy and more tired.
I've never had high blood pressure.
I don't have diabetes.

facts.item: high blood pressure in the family
facts.text: No one in my family has high blood pressure.
No one in my family has diabetes.
I haven't fainted.
I haven't had any neurological symptoms.
My joints don't hurt.
I haven't had any problems with my body's automatic functions (autonomic symptoms).

findings.name: lung examination
findings.result: Bibasilar dullness and decreased air entry, more on the right.

findings.name: heart examination
findings.result: Quiet precordium; systolic murmur at the left sternal border.

findings.name: abdominal examination
findings.result: Tender liver enlarged 6 cm below the costal margin; shifting dullness.

findings.name: abdominal ultrasound
findings.result: Hepatic congestion with hepatomegaly, ascites and bilateral pleural effusions.

findings.name: electrocardiogram
findings.result: Low-voltage limb leads with a pseudoinfarction pattern in the precordial leads; ST-segment depression with T-wave inversions in V4–V6.

findings.name: transthoracic echocardiography
findings.result: Biatrial enlargement and biventricular hypertrophy (IVS 22 mm, LVPW 21 mm, RV wall 14 mm) with interatrial septal thickening and granular 'sparkling' myocardium. LVEF 65% with no regional wall motion abnormalities. Doppler: restrictive filling pattern (E/A ratio 11, septal e′ 3, E/e′ 18) and atrial arrest. Mitral, aortic and tricuspid valves thickened; plethoric IVC; minimal pericardial effusion.

gold.reasoning: 1. Hypertensive heart disease considered but excluded — “lack of a previous or current history of hypertension ... and the presence of a low voltage ECG instead of ECG features of left ventricular hypertrophy ... suggest that hypertensive heart disease is less likely in this case.” 2. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy considered but excluded — “presence of right ventricular hypertrophy ... and thickening of the interatrial septum ... make HCM less likely in this patient even without diagnostic imaging such as CMR.” 3. Cardiac amyloidosis considered most likely — “typical low voltage QRS with a pseudo infarction pattern, along with echocardiographic features such as LVH (ECG‐echocardiography discordance), biventricular hypertrophy, biatrial enlargement, interatrial septal thickening, myocardial sparkling, restrictive LV filling, and typical atrial arrest on echocardiography with persistent elevation of cardiac troponin ... strongly indicate cardiac amyloidosis.”

quotes.f002: progressively worsening shortness of breath over 1 month
quotes.f012: enalapril caused dizziness and worsened fatigue

f008: The source does not say whether furosemide and enalapril are still being taken; no time given.
f018: Blanket denial ('neurologic symptoms'); answers only an open question about nerve or brain symptoms, not specific ones.
f020: Blanket denial ('autonomic symptoms'); specific autonomic questions stay unknown. Enalapril-related dizziness (f012) is a side effect, not denied here.

x017: E/A ratio 11 with 'atrial arrest' is internally odd (atrial arrest implies little or no A wave); reported as given.

source_issues: The echocardiogram reports an E/A ratio of 11 together with atrial arrest; values reported as given.
No confirmatory test (cardiac MRI, scintigraphy, biopsy, light chains) is reported; the diagnosis rests on ECG and echocardiography.
notes: Index visit: the emergency presentation with a month of worsening breathlessness, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea and leg swelling (s001-s017); the furosemide and enalapril were given before this visit (s003).
The examination and test names avoid the word 'cardiac' (a gold term): 'heart examination', 'troponin'.
